faqs.a: No — fewer than 0.1% of US estates owe any federal estate tax. With a $15 million per-person exemption in 2026, the tax touches only very large estates. If your total assets are under the exemption, your federal bill is zero and no return is even required.
faqs.q: Do most people pay estate tax?

faqs.a: Yes, under current law. The 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act replaced the temporary doubled exemption with a permanent $15 million base starting 2026, indexed for inflation from 2027. A future Congress could always change it, but no sunset is scheduled.

Nearly everything you own at death: real estate, investments, bank accounts, business interests, personal property — and life insurance proceeds if you owned the policy. Debts, funeral costs, and transfers to a spouse or charity are deductible before the exemption applies.
faqs.q: What counts in my gross estate?

faqs.a: No — the estate pays it before anything is distributed. Heirs receive what's left. (Separately, about a dozen states impose their own estate or inheritance taxes, and a few tax the heirs directly on inheritances.)
faqs.q: Do heirs pay the estate tax?

faqs.a: Yes, with proper planning. Each spouse gets a $15 million exemption, and portability lets a surviving spouse use the deceased spouse's unused portion. Credit-shelter trusts achieve the same. Without portability or trust planning, the second $15M can be wasted.
faqs.q: Can a married couple shield $30 million?

faqs.a: Common tools: annual tax-free gifts ($19,000 per recipient in 2026), irrevocable life insurance trusts, charitable trusts, family limited partnerships, and lifetime use of the exemption. All require advance planning with an estate attorney — this calculator just sizes the problem.
faqs.q: How can large estates reduce the tax?

estate-tax-calculator.formula:
Taxable estate = gross estate - exemption - deductions (never below zero).
Estimated tax = taxable estate x 40%.
Example: (20,000,000 - 15,000,000) x 40% = $2,000,000.
howTo: Enter the total estate value (all assets at fair market value).
Check the exemption — $15M per person for 2026, adjustable.
Enter deductible debts and expenses, if any.
Read the taxable estate and estimated federal tax.
keyFacts: The 2026 federal exemption is $15 million per individual ($30M per couple with portability).
Only the amount above the exemption is taxed — never the whole estate.
The top federal rate is 40% on the taxable amount.
The exemption is now permanent (2025 law), indexed for inflation from 2027.
About a dozen states add their own estate or inheritance taxes with lower thresholds.

estate-tax-calculator.quickAnswer: In 2026, the federal estate tax exemption is $15 million per person. A $20 million estate with no deductions has a $5 million taxable estate, taxed at 40% = $2 million. Below the exemption, the federal bill is zero — and fewer than 0.1% of estates ever owe it.
estate-tax-calculator.tagline: Estimate US federal estate tax — exemption, taxable estate, and the 40% top rate.
estate-tax-calculator.workedExample:
Estate $20,000,000, exemption $15,000,000, deductions $0:
1. Taxable estate = 20,000,000 - 15,000,000 - 0 = $5,000,000.
2. Estimated tax = 5,000,000 x 40% = $2,000,000.
3. Effective rate on the whole estate = 2,000,000 / 20,000,000 = 10%.
4. An estate of $14M would owe $0 — below the exemption.
